hints.title: Bijection One-to-One Character Mapping
hints.text: Two strings are isomorphic if characters in s can be replaced to get t while preserving order. How can checking both directions ensure no two characters map to the same target?

hints.title: Last Seen Index Alignment Invariant
hints.text: Characters s[i] and t[i] must share identical last seen positions throughout the string traversal.

hints.title: Dual Index Character Tracking Procedure
hints.text: Maintain two lookup arrays recording the last seen index plus 1 for characters in s and t. Traverse index i from 0 to length - 1: if last seen index of s[i] does not equal last seen index of t[i], return false. Update both records to i + 1. Return true if loop finishes.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Verifying mapping in only one direction permits multiple characters to map to the same destination character.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Dual 256-entry index tracking evaluates bijection in O(N) time with O(1) auxiliary alphabet storage.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that isomorphic equivalence requires a bijective (two-way) mapping.
